question: We make an aqueous mixture of certified FD&C straight colors preserved with sodium benzoate. Can it be certified for food, drug and cosmetic use?
answer: The FDA requires that certified color additives be declared by their name in the applicable regulations, unless otherwise specified. For example, a certified color additive may be listed by a specific or abbreviated name such as "FD&C Blue No. 1" or "Blue 1." The declaration must include the term "Lake" for the lake of the certified color additive. Additionally, if the color additive is used in food or cosmetics, it must be declared as "Artificial Color," "Artificial Color Added," or "Color Added" (or an equivalent term). If the color additive is not subject to certification and not otherwise required by applicable regulations, it may be declared as "Artificial Color," "Artificial Color Added," or "Color Added." The requirement applies to the common or usual name of the color additive. If the color additive is for external application to shell eggs or for use in coloring a food specified in the requests for certification, the diluent (except sodium benzoate) must be removed and not become a component of the food. The requirement applies to the usual process of manufacturing such food. [4]

claim_candidates.text: The FDA requires that certified color additives be declared by their name in the applicable regulations, unless otherwise specified.
For example, a certified color additive may be listed by a specific or abbreviated name such as "FD&C Blue No. 1" or "Blue 1."
The declaration must include the term "Lake" for the lake of the certified color additive.
Additionally, if the color additive is used in food or cosmetics, it must be declared as "Artificial Color," "Artificial Color Added," or "Color Added" (or an equivalent term).
If the color additive is not subject to certification and not otherwise required by applicable regulations, it may be declared as "Artificial Color," "Artificial Color Added," or "Color Added."
The requirement applies to the common or usual name of the color additive.

If the color additive is for external application to shell eggs or for use in coloring a food specified in the requests for certification, the diluent (except sodium benzoate) must be removed and not become a component of the food.
The requirement applies to the usual process of manufacturing such food [4].
